subject: Request: SLA exception for large async backfill (completion window, retries, idempotency)
messages:

Cc: procurement@greengrid.io
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Large historic backfill — need SLA exception and guidance

Hi Karthik,

We kicked off a large async inference backfill over the weekend against our historical orders (approx 18M rows). Early telemetry suggests a lot of long-running jobs are being queued and a handful of runs are exceeding the 24h completion window we assumed in our contract. Procurement is copying me asking whether we can get an exception to the standard job completion SLA while we finish the first phased backfill.

Specifically we need:
- Temporary SLA exception for job completion window to 72 hours for the next 2 weeks (we can provision burst capacity but want this clause for billing/credits).
- Guidance on best practice for retries and dedup/idempotency so we don't double-process records if a job restarts.
- Any changes to retry/backoff policy that Redwood recommends for high-volume historical runs.

Attached is a short summary of the backfill and estimated run sizes. Can you advise quickly? We are on a tight procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Akira
Akira Tanaka
Director, Data Platform
Acme Commerce

Akira — thanks for the note and the summary. Short answer: we can support a temporary exception, but we need to lock down operational controls (idempotency, retry limits, and monitoring) and an explicit credit/penalty clause for missed completion windows.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Can you confirm the expected peak concurrent jobs and average TTL per job (approx tokens/rows per request)?
2) We'll require an idempotency_key per record/batch and recommend per-job level dedup windows of 7 days for this backfill.
3) For retries: limit to 3 automatic attempts with exponential backoff (initial 30s, 5m, 30m) and then surface to manual retry. That avoids thundering herd on transient infra issues.
4) We can provision a temporary SLA exception to 72h for job completion for a 14-day window subject to: a) agreed idempotency approach, b) a capped retry policy, and c) a one-time runbook/war room during the first 48h.

I will loop in Neha (solutions) and Laura (customer success / credits) to document the operational checklist and draft the exception language. If you can share expected concurrency numbers today, we can get procurement a draft addendum by EOD.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi all — added some technical details below based on what we see works for similar customers. Akira — copying the suggested implementation so your infra team can evaluate quickly.

Implementation notes (recommended):
- Idempotency: require a client-supplied idempotency_key at the batch unit (we recommend per-1000-record chunk). Redwood will persist idempotency keys for 14 days for backfill runs. If a key is re-submitted within the window we return the original job id and status.
- Retry policy: automatic retry up to 3 failures. Backoff schedule: 30s, 5m, 30m. After 3 attempts the job moves to FAILED_MANUAL_RETRY. Manual retries can be run via the Console or API with a distinct idempotency_key.
- Partial failures: for very large units we recommend splitting into smaller chunks (<=50k records) to reduce per-job variance and improve parallelism.
- Observability: enable per-job trace logs and add a short-lived forwarder that streams error-level logs to your S3 bucket for the 72h window. We can assist with a CloudWatch->S3 connector.

Operational ask from Acme: please add metadata headers in the call: X-Acme-Run-Id and X-Acme-Chunk-Seq so we can map jobs back to source records.

I'll draft the operational checklist and exception wording once we have the concurrency numbers.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Akira — quick note on credits/exception terms from CS/finance:
- Exception duration: 14 days starting when the first bulk job is flagged for the exception (we will record the start timestamp).
- Completion window: 72 hours per job for that period. If a job exceeds 72 hours due to Redwood service issues (not client-side suspensions), Acme will be eligible for a pro-rata service credit: 1% of monthly invoice per missed job up to a max of 10% for the exception window.
- If missed completions exceed 5% of total backfill job count, we will arrange a joint post-mortem and additional credit (to be negotiated).

Please confirm you accept these guardrails and we'll attach an addendum to the SOW. Also: Akira — can you share the peak concurrency numbers so we can validate capacity?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
